title: Comparing length and weight
examples: Teacher, how do I know which toy is heavier?
Can we compare the length of these two crayons?
If I put things on the scale, what does it tell me?

explain.say: Look at these two sticks. Say which one is longer. This stick is longer than that stick.
Now look at these two ribbons. Say which one is shorter. This ribbon is shorter than that ribbon.
Next, we look at weight. Say which block is heavier. This block is heavier than that block.
We can use a balance scale to compare weight. If one side goes down, it is heavier.
When you bring your toys to school, you might compare their lengths. You see a long crayon and a short one. You can tell which crayon is longer than the other.

faq.q: How do I know if something is longer?
faq.a: You can line the two things up next to each other. The one that stretches out more is longer.
No, 'heavy' means it has a lot of weight. A big feather can still be very light.
asks: What is the difference between big and heavy?

faq.q: What does the balance scale show?
faq.a: The scale shows which side has more weight. The side that sinks down is the heavier one.
asks: How do I use the scale?
What does it mean if the scale tips?

faq.q: Can I compare things that are not straight?
faq.a: You can still compare them by looking at their longest part. We compare the space they take up.
asks: Do I have to line them up?

faq.q: If the scale is level, what does that mean?
faq.a: If the scale is level, it means both things weigh exactly the same. They have the same weight.

facts: Longer means something takes up more space in a line.
Shorter means something takes up less space in a line.
Heavier means something has more weight.
Lighter means something has less weight.
A balance scale helps us compare weights.

quiz.say: Which is longer, a pencil or a ruler?
quiz.why: A ruler is usually longer than a standard pencil.

wrong.0: This is wrong because they are different objects.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you can compare them easily.
wrong.3: This is tempting because pencils are easy to see.

quiz.say: If a feather and a rock are on the scale, and the rock side goes down, what is true?
quiz.why: When the rock side goes down, it means it has more weight.

wrong.1: This is wrong because the scale shows the rock is heavier.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the scale is tipped down.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the scale is showing a difference.

quiz.say: Which word means something has less weight?
quiz.why: Lighter is the word we use for something with less weight.

wrong.0: This word can mean size, but 'lighter' is best for weight.
wrong.1: This is too general; 'lighter' is the specific word for weight.
wrong.3: This word describes length, not weight.
